name: Siemens Energy
legalName: Siemens Energy AG (rebranding to 'Omterra' — announced July 14, 2026, phase-in from late 2026)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Siemens Energy is one of the two Western giants (with GE Vernova) that gate the AIDC buildout's two scarcest inputs — gas turbines and grid equipment — and it is monetizing that chokehold at record levels: group backlog hit €162B at June 30, 2026, Gas Services booked €10.0B of orders in a single quarter (book-to-bill 2.65, 73 turbines = 15 GW) with US data centers the named driver, and Q3 FY26 delivered the highest quarterly group margin in company history (14.2%). The 500 MW SGT-800-based standard block co-developed with Eaton is its purpose-built AIDC onsite-power product. BACKGROUND: Spun off from Siemens AG in 2020, the company nearly collapsed in 2023 when Siemens Gamesa wind-turbine defects (15-30% of the newest onshore fleets) forced a €2.2B charge, a ~€4.5B net loss, and a €7.5B German federal counter-guarantee — a state rescue fully replaced by a €9B private bank facility in June 2025, two years early. The recovery since is one of Europe's great re-ratings (~593% three-year return; record €191.66 in April 2026), which cuts both ways: the stock trades near 70x earnings and fell on the Q3 FY26 beat. A rebrand to 'Omterra' was announced July 14, 2026 — the Siemens name is licensed and time-limited.
ecosystemRole: We assess Siemens Energy as the AIDC sector's most complete grid-plus-generation supplier — the only vendor that can deliver the gas turbines, the transformers, the switchgear, the HVDC, and the grid-stability equipment for a gigawatt campus from one book. Basis: a top-3 global gas-turbine position (with GE Vernova and Mitsubishi Power, roughly two-thirds of turbines for plants under construction; note Mitsubishi held #1 MW share in 2022-23 per McCoy), Grid Technologies backlog of €51B with transformers as the biggest growth driver, and the Eaton alliance packaging a repeatable 500 MW grid-independent block that 'eliminates diesel backup gensets' and claims two years off time-to-power. Its capacity decisions are sector-wide constraints: large-frame slots are 'nearly full' for 2028, reservation fees are back for the first time since the early-2000s boom, and the +30-50% expansion in transformers and turbines over FY26-28 is the sector's supply-relief valve.

productsAndServices.name: Gas Services — turbine portfolio (2-593 MW)
productsAndServices.description: Full-line gas turbine OEM: heavy-duty HL class (SGT5-9000HL 593 MW / SGT6-9000HL 440 MW), H/F/E classes, industrial units (SGT-800 flagship, 45-62 MW), and aeroderivatives (SGT-A35). FY25: 194 turbines sold (vs 100 in FY24); Q3 FY26 booked 73 turbines (25 large, 48 industrial) totaling 15 GW. Medium-turbine annual capacity being lifted from ~50 to ~80 units; large-GT and transformer capacity each expanding +30-50% over FY26-28.
productsAndServices.positioning: Top-3 globally with GE Vernova and Mitsubishi Power; the SGT-800 is the workhorse of the data-center onsite-power segment (620 installations, >20M operating hours, 99.1% reliability); SGT6-9000HL is the direct 7HA.03 rival at >64% combined-cycle efficiency.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct to utilities, IPPs, and data-center developers; long-term service agreements; slot-reservation fees now standard.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Gas Services backlog €73B; large-frame slots nearly full through 2028; Charlotte, NC gas-turbine manufacturing resuming as part of the $1B US investment (Feb 2026).

productsAndServices.name: Grid Technologies — transformers, switchgear, HVDC, grid stability
productsAndServices.description: Power transformers 10 kV-800 kV / 10-1,300 MVA (incl. HVDC converter transformers), distribution transformers, GIS/AIS switchgear incl. the SF6-free 'Blue' portfolio and DC-GIS to ±550 kV, HVDC PLUS (VSC), E-STATCOM (marketed specifically for data-center load fluctuation), synchronous condensers, and the Qstor BESS / BlueVault storage lines. Q3 FY26: orders €5.4B (+28%), revenue +29%, margin 19.9%, backlog €51B — transformers the largest growth contributor, data centers a named driver.
productsAndServices.positioning: One of the few Western vendors addressing the transformer bottleneck (US Southeast lead times 36+ months; ~80% of US large power transformers imported) with domestic capacity: $150M Charlotte LPT plant (first units early 2026, full production 2027) and a new Mississippi HV switchgear plant.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct to utilities, grid operators, and hyperscale campus developers; framework agreements.
productsAndServices.roadmap: €220M Nuremberg transformer factory plus brownfield expansions (US, India, Croatia, Austria, Saudi Arabia, Brazil); ~1/3 of the €6B FY26-28 capex program goes to transformers/switchgear.

productsAndServices.name: Modular on-site power for data centers (Eaton alliance)
productsAndServices.description: Standardized, repeatable grid-independent power blocks for campuses >100 MW: redundant SGT-800 turbines + battery storage, eliminating diesel backup gensets, 99.99%+ availability, ~50% CO2 reduction vs traditional approaches, claimed up to two years off time-to-power. The June 2025 Eaton alliance defines a 500 MW standard configuration — Siemens Energy supplies generation/storage, Eaton the grid-to-chip electrical stack (MV/LV switchgear, UPS, busway, racks).
productsAndServices.positioning: The direct competitive answer to GE Vernova's turbine-plus-electrification AIDC offers; differentiated by the diesel-elimination claim and SGT-800 fleet track record; hydrogen-ready (SGT-800 to 75 vol% H2).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Joint go-to-market with Eaton; direct EPC-partnered delivery.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Q3 FY26 Gas Services intake included 'large orders related to data centers' in the US; optional later grid connection and future hydrogen operation are the block's upgrade path.

productsAndServices.name: Siemens Gamesa (wind) & Transformation of Industry
productsAndServices.description: Siemens Gamesa: onshore/offshore wind — Q3 FY26 was its first profitable quarter since FY2022 (+€75M before special items) after the 2023 blade/bearing quality crisis; 90% of the Indian wind business divested to a TPG-led group. Transformation of Industry: compression, electrolyzers, industrial steam turbines (to 1,900 MW), PEM fuel cells.
productsAndServices.positioning: Wind is the recovering drag, not the growth story — backlog €31B but segment FCF still negative (-€518M in the profitable Q3); TI is steady mid-margin industrial business.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Segment targeted to break even for full FY2026; onshore 4.X/5.X platforms gradually resuming after the defect halt.

recentDevelopments.headline: Q3 FY26: record orders (€17.9B), record revenue, highest quarterly group margin in company history (14.2%) — and the stock fell
recentDevelopments.read: Net income €1.19B beat consensus by ~21%; Gas Services book-to-bill hit 2.65 with US data-center orders the named driver; Siemens Gamesa posted its first profitable quarter since FY2022. Shares slipped anyway — priced-to-perfection risk at ~70x earnings is the live debate, not execution.

recentDevelopments.headline: Rebrand announced: Siemens Energy and Siemens Gamesa to unite as 'Omterra' from late 2026
recentDevelopments.read: The Siemens trademark is licensed and time-limited; the rebrand asserts independence from the parent. Practical note for anyone tracking the vendor: name, branding, and possibly ticker references change within months.

recentDevelopments.headline: $1B US investment, 1,500+ jobs: Mississippi HV switchgear plant, Charlotte gas-turbine manufacturing resumption, Orlando AI grid lab with NVIDIA
recentDevelopments.read: Aggressive localization against both the transformer bottleneck (~80% of US LPTs imported, 36+ month lead times) and tariff exposure. Charlotte LPT production starts 2026-27 — the US supply response lags the demand spike by design-build reality, not intent.

recentDevelopments.headline: Capital Market Day: FY28 margin target raised to 14-16%, €6B buyback, up to €10B shareholder returns, +30-50% capacity expansion in transformers and turbines
recentDevelopments.read: The supply-side decision that matters most to the AIDC sector: Siemens Energy is the relief valve for turbine and transformer scarcity, and it chose measured expansion plus shareholder returns over a maximal capacity race — supporting pricing power but prolonging the bottleneck. Shares +8.4% to record highs on the day.

recentDevelopments.headline: FY25 results beat: orders €58.9B, net income €1.7B, first dividend in four years; 194 turbines sold vs 100 in FY24
recentDevelopments.read: The turnaround completed all commitments two years after near-collapse. Citigroup: targets 'exceeded the already high market expectations.' The unit-sales doubling is the cleanest single measure of the gas-power demand shock.

recentDevelopments.headline: Xcel Energy orders 10× SGT6-5000F (2,088 MW) for Texas — 'dispatchable power is no longer optional'
recentDevelopments.read: Utility-scale validation of the F-class in the exact geography (Texas Panhandle) where data-center load growth is straining the grid; replaces retired coal with first deliveries in early 2026.

recentDevelopments.headline: Eaton alliance: joint fast-track data-center offering with a 500 MW SGT-800-based standard onsite-power block
recentDevelopments.read: The productized AIDC play — grid-independent at day one, optional grid connection later, no diesel gensets, claimed two years off time-to-power. Pairs Siemens Energy generation with Eaton's grid-to-chip electrical stack; a direct structural answer to GE Vernova's AIDC push.

recentDevelopments.headline: €9B five-year facility from 23 international banks fully replaces the German federal counter-guarantee — state-rescue chapter closed two years early
recentDevelopments.read: Removes the last overhang from the 2023 crisis. The speed of the exit (private banks re-underwriting the guarantee book) is the strongest external validation of the turnaround's credibility.

strategyRead: (High confidence) Siemens Energy (with GE Vernova and Mitsubishi Power) effectively sets the AIDC sector's time-to-power floor: large-frame slots nearly full through 2028, reservation fees back for the first time since the early-2000s boom, and a deliberate +30-50% (not maximal) capacity expansion. Anyone selling into gas-powered AIDC campuses is planning around this company's delivery calendar. Basis: company CMD disclosures, POWER/Bloomberg supply-crunch reporting, Q3 FY26 book-to-bill 2.65.

(High confidence) The Eaton alliance's 500 MW SGT-800 block is the most productized onsite-power offering from any major OEM — a standardized, diesel-free, hydrogen-ready package aimed squarely at the behind-the-meter demand xAI, Crusoe, and the hyperscalers have validated. Basis: company-published alliance specification; Q3 FY26 US data-center orders confirm commercial traction.

(Moderate confidence) The grid side (Grid Technologies, €51B backlog, 19.9% margin) is the more durable franchise than gas turbines: transformer scarcity outlasts any single generation cycle, ~80% of installed transformer capacity in advanced economies reaches age limits by 2035, and Siemens Energy is one of only a handful of vendors localizing US production. Basis: company capacity disclosures and third-party lead-time data; the 2035 aging claim is company market framing.

(Moderate confidence) Valuation is the principal risk to reading momentum as strength: ~70x earnings, DCF fair-value estimates as low as €29 vs a ~€150-190 price, an €84-vs-€175 sell-side target chasm, and a stock that fell on a 21% earnings beat. If AIDC buildout pace slows, today's book-to-bill and capacity expansion become cyclical exposure — the same dynamic that burned turbine OEMs after the early-2000s gas boom. Basis: third-party analyst coverage; explicitly a market judgment, not an operational one.

(Low confidence) Wind remains the fragility: one profitable quarter after 15 straight losses, still-negative segment cash flow, and a defect history (15-30% of newest onshore fleets) that argues for caution on execution claims until several clean quarters accumulate. A wind relapse would not threaten the company as in 2023 (the guarantee structure is now private), but it would dent the FY28 margin path.
